page.layout: One printed page, right side of scan: ornamental printer's rule, centred heading block, then verse paragraphs in italic with a decorated initial. Faint show-through of the facing page (EPISTOLA heading and text) at the right edge is not transcribed.

main_text.head: IN CATONIS DISTICHA Carmen PAVLI LENTVLI.
main_text.p: PLurima de Cælo quamuis dimi-serit alto Auxilia, omnipotens, tempus in om-ne, Deus.

p.i: Queis virtutis iter Mortales carpere possent,
Ducere & innocuos et sine labe dies.
Ast ingrata tamen, cæcóque impulsa furore,
Mens hominum pergit turpia facta sequi.
Ascræus fuit ante senex, fuit ante cicutâ Attica, quem letho turba scelesta dedit.
Et fuit eximius Samiæ telluris Alumnus Cecrop

page.notes: The initial "P" is a decorative woodcut letter; read as P. Show-through text from the reverse (EPISTOLA, "mortalis", "scelus" lines) is ignored. "Ducere &" follows the printed ampersand form. Last line is cut off at the page foot as printed: "Cecrop" with the rest of the word not visible.
